title: Synthesis and Engineering of Functional Graphene Films for Matrix-Free LDI Mass Spectrometry Detection
protocol: Mix concentrated sulphuric acid and fuming nitric acid.
Cool the mixture in an ice-water bath.
Add graphite under stirring into the cooled acid mixture.
Slowly add KClO3 over more than 15 minutes while stirring carefully.
Pour the resulting mixture into water, filter it completely, and wash to obtain graphite oxides after stirring for 96 hours at room temperature.
Mix ethylene glycol, water, and PEG-2000.
Disperse graphite oxide in the mixed solution.
Sonicate the mixture for two hours to form a homogeneous graphene oxide suspension.
Transfer the whole suspension into a Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave.
React the suspension at 180°C for 24 hours to perform solvent thermal reduction of graphene oxide to graphene sheets.
Filter 50 mL of reacted mixture using a commercial vacuum filtration device and dry it for 24 hours at room temperature to form the film product.
Carefully remove the as-made film from the filtration device to avoid potential damage.
Place the free-standing graphene film on a commercial MALDI plate from Bruker for laser engineering.
Use a pulsed nitrogen laser with wavelength of 337 nm and frequency of 200 Hz in the Bruker Autoflex III MS chamber.
Set up imaging mode, where spot-to-spot distance is set to be 30 µm and 500 shots were taken at each spot.
Set the laser intensity to be 50% (about 121.8 µJ for 100%) for laser engineering.
Prepare diluted analyte solutions in a step-wise manner.
Stock the diluted analyte solutions at -20°C before use.
Deposit 0.4 μL of analytes on the engineered area for drying.
Obtain mass spectra via an accumulation of 500 laser shots under a laser intensity of 36% for data collection.
Use standard peptides, Angiotensin II (M.W. 1046.5) and ACTH-Clip (M.W. 2465.7), for molecular weight calibration.
